newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity hits highs on physical strength.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity hits highs on physical strength.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures continued to climb Tuesday, reaching new highs based on strong Western physical power prices, industry sources said.
"We're in a peak period and you don't store this (electricity), so you can't store the current stock and buy the out months," a New York-based power futures trader said.
As of 1245 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures were trading up 67 cents at $22.05 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $22.15 and trade as low as $21.70 per MWh.

July PV was trading up 60 cents at a new contract high of $25.45 after hitting a new contract high of $25.50 and trade as low as $25.25, while November was up 25 cents at a new contract high of $19.75 per MWh.

June California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 45 cents at $15.90 per MWh after hitting a new contract high of $16.15 and trading as low as $15.90, while July was bid at $17.25 from Monday's settle at $16.90 per MWh.
September COB was up 30 cents at a new contract high of $20.40 per MWh.

The jump was attributed to strong Western power prices driven primarily by cooling demand in the Southwest, where peak tempertures were forecast to reach over 100 degrees Fahrenheit in parts of Arizona today.
The COB futures were said to be following in sympathy with the PV contracts.
Several generation plant outages in the West were also giving price support, the industry sources said.

Generation capacity in the western U.S. remained limited, with about 8,000 megawatts in the West said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of the idled capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
Restart of the 550 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired power complex in Wyoming was delayed to Wednesday from Sunday.
Peak physical Western power was said to be mostly flat Tuesday for Wednesday delivery, with COB power pegged at $16.50-17.00 and PV near $23.50-24.00, sources said.
NYMEX said as of 1205 an estimated total of 399 COB and 140 PV contracts had traded.

In the Northwest, temperatures were forecast to average above normal through Sunday, while in the Southwest temperatures were expected to be six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Sunday, with little or no precipitation.
COB open interest for May 5 rose 168 to 4,835, while PV open interest rose 85 to 5,659, NYMEX said.
